gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-cactus-classical-se: Aaargh draws tubelike, constant-weight lines with a generous opening into every e. But Cactus Classical Serif moves like a lightly tilted nib, so paragraphs would flow with a soft, steady variation.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-caudex: Aaargh holds its bowls at the exact thickness of its stems, a strong display voice with nothing tapering. Caudex gapes wide on the e and keeps its thin strokes just under the thick ones, dignified and readable.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-chiron-sung-hk: Commanding up top, Aaargh keeps its tube-like thickness through every bend. That heading stands out with unbroken weight, while Chiron Sung HK quietly does its work through light modulation and wide-set curve ends.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-cinzel: Strong and tubelike, Aaargh never varies its stroke width. Cinzel, a serif set loosely with space to spare, adds joins that taper modestly, so the heading's solid pipes stand over finer, more spaced lettering.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-diphylleia: Diphylleia reads classic and bookish, with openings that hold up at tiny sizes. And the pair's real pull is the gap between Aaargh, which has no stroke contrast at all, and a body where stems slightly outweigh hairlines.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-donegal-one: Donegal One leaves daylight in its curves and never turns spindly. Aaargh does its best work with a wire-like monoline skeleton, while Donegal One saves its effort for a subtle weight change like etched lines in glass.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-fjord-one: Round letters whose rims match their stems give Aaargh its tubelike, commanding look up top. And Fjord One, a serif with wide-mouthed rounds, softens each curve with a gentle weight change and no harsh thin spots.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-gentium-book-plus: Traditional in manner, Gentium Book Plus sets its horizontals a notch lighter. Yet Aaargh has no stroke variation in any letter, so its heading lands as a solid mass over body text of moderate contrast.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-gfs-didot: Aaargh never lets bold-looking and light-looking strokes mix within a word, so its display heading stays one solid, commanding voice. Against that, GFS Didot adds a modest stem-to-hairline ratio, the pair's real edge.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-im-fell-english-sc: Aaargh excels at strokes of constant width in every letter, like bent pipe. But IM Fell English SC does its best work through slight but noticeable contrast and generously open throats.
